title: Genetic data and the law

blocks.what_we_do:
Reading, about 2 minutes. You can come back to it later.

Learn the main legal points before you upload genetic data. This step is information, not legal advice.
blocks.why:
Before you upload real data, speak to the data protection officer of your institution.

- Genotypes are personal data even without names. A genome is unique, and a few hundred SNPs are enough to identify a person.
- Under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), genetic data are a special category. Processing them needs a specific legal basis, for example research with appropriate safeguards and consent.
- A transfer of personal data outside the EU needs an additional legal basis: for example an adequacy decision for the destination country, or contractual clauses approved by the European Commission. Whether a given server qualifies is a legal question. The answer can change over time.
- Consent forms and ethics approvals may also limit where data can go. Many European cohorts do not allow upload to servers outside the EU.
- An EU server such as HMIS removes the transfer problem. It does not remove your other duties: a legal basis, data minimisation and a contract with the processor.

**Good practice before any upload.**

1. Upload only what imputation needs: genotypes and sample IDs. Never upload phenotypes, names or dates of birth.
2. Replace real IDs with codes that only you can link back.
3. Keep a record of what you uploaded, where and when.
4. Download the results promptly and keep the password safe.

**In this course** the data are simulated. They describe no real person. You may upload them to any server to practise, with no legal risk. The course examples do not do so, for a scientific reason (see the module overview): the server panels contain the donors of the simulation.

Reference: [Rayner et al. 2024](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41588-024-02012-1).
blocks.command: No code to run. This is a reading-only step.
blocks.expected_result: You can list what to check with your institution before an upload.
blocks.troubleshooting: If you are not sure whether an upload is allowed, do not upload. Ask the data protection officer and the principal investigator of the study.
blocks.quick_check:
A colleague removes the names from a file of genotypes and says that the file is now anonymous. Is that right?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. A genome is unique, and a few hundred SNPs can identify a person. Genotypes remain personal data without names.

</details>

student_summary: We see why genotypes are personal data under the European General Data Protection Regulation, what a transfer outside the EU needs, and what to do before any upload.
